title: New Housing, Land and Construction Rules Taking Effect in 2027
desc: Summary of 2027 rules: amended Notarisation Law, QCVN 01:2026, end of the 50% fee reduction, construction practice certificates, registration fee.
summary: Changes on notarisation, planning, fees, practice certificates and registration fees applying from 1 January 2027 and 1 March 2027 that property buyers, sellers and home builders should know.
body: p

In 2027 a number of new documents begin to apply or reach the end of their application period. Below are the main changes relating to buying and selling property and building houses, covering only documents whose full text is in the Quan Construction legal library.
h2
1. From 1 January 2027: the amended Notarisation Law
p
Law No. 04/2026/QH16 amends the 2024 Notarisation Law and takes effect on 1 January 2027. Some points that property buyers and sellers should know (Article 1):
ul
Notarisation is defined as a public service; transactions that must be notarised are those the law requires to be notarised, and the Ministry of Justice publishes the list on its web portal.
Papers in the dossier may be paper copies, electronic copies or electronic originals; information already in a published database need not be submitted as a document.

Notarisation of real estate transactions remains within the province or centrally run city where the notarial organisation is headquartered; the Government will prescribe a roadmap for nationwide notarisation.

The provincial People's Committee may transfer the authority to certify transactions from the commune-level People's Committee Chairperson to notarial practice organisations in communes that already have a notarial organisation meeting requirements.
p
For details, see Amended Notarisation Law: what is new from 2027.
h2
2. From 1 January 2027: QCVN 01:2026/BXD replaces QCVN 01:2021/BXD
p

The national technical regulation on urban and rural planning issued with Circular 46/2026/TT-BXD takes effect on 1 January 2027. Some indicators relating to single-family houses: maximum net building density by plot area and a land use coefficient not exceeding 7 times (Section 2.5.3); the minimum number of car parking spaces for newly developed single-family house groups (Section 2.8.4.13). Plans approved before 1 January 2027 continue to be implemented until their term ends (Section 5.4.1).
p
See Building density and setbacks for houses under QCVN 01:2026.
h2
3. From 1 January 2027: the 50% reduction ends for many fees and charges
p

Circular 64/2025/TT-BTC reduces many fees and charges by 50% from 1 July 2025 to 31 December 2026. From 1 January 2027, the rates return to those in the original circulars (Clause 2, Article 1), including:
ul
Fee for appraising fire prevention and fighting designs;
Fee for issuing a construction activity practice certificate;
Fee for appraising technical designs and fee for appraising construction cost estimates;
Fee for appraising construction investment projects.
h2
4. From 1 March 2027: change in positions that must hold a practice certificate
p

Law 24/2026/QH16 amends Clauses 1 and 2, Article 88 of the Construction Law 2025: the positions of lead person for determining, appraising and managing construction investment costs no longer need a practice certificate; Clause 2 now lists only the project management director and the site chief commander. According to the library list, Resolution 66.18/2026/NQ-CP, which relates to this content, applies until the end of 28 February 2027.
h2
5. From 1 March 2027: registration fee - a change only for electric cars
p

Decree 202/2026/ND-CP takes effect on 1 March 2027 and replaces Decree 51/2025/ND-CP. The amendment is a first-time registration fee rate of 0% for battery electric cars until the end of 31 December 2030 (Article 1). This Decree does not change the registration fee for houses and land; the 0.5% rate still follows Article 8 of Consolidated Document 33/VBHN-BTC.
h2
6. What homeowners should do in early 2027
ol
Before notarising a sale, check whether your papers already exist in electronic form or the information is in the database, to reduce paper dossiers.
When designing and applying for a building permit, ask the design firm for the planning indicators that apply to the plot (density, setback, number of floors).
Budget for appraisal fees at the full rate if the work is subject to appraisal.
Check the practice certificates of the designer and supervisor you hire.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. It covers only documents in the Quan Construction library at the time of writing; the 2024 Notarisation Law has been amended by Law 106/2025/QH15 (full text not yet in the library); Resolution 66.18/2026/NQ-CP does not yet have its full text. Check for documents issued after the date of this article.
